title: TUI queue columns are configurable
lead: A `tui.columns` config key lists which queue columns the TUI shows and in what order, so an owner can trade the claim, size or score cells for title room.
findings_note: owner, 2026-10-15, s277 relay: asked whether the queue's columns could be chosen by the user after the claim column crowded titles at 80 columns; s277 shipped a fixed rule (claim capped at 8 cells, size dropped below a 50-cell pane)
boundary: **Not in this slice:** columns in `slicer list` text, new column kinds, and per-session toggles in the TUI.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: s277 added a claim cell to the queue row (`#  ID  status  size  P:score  title`). At 80 columns the queue pane is 38 cells, so every fixed cell costs title room. The owner asked for user-chosen columns on 2026-10-15 and accepted a fixed rule for v1.11.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/config.py`: `tui.columns`, a list drawn from `claim`, `size`, `score`, validated like other list keys; the default reproduces s277's layout.
- `src/slicer/tui.py`: `item_rows` builds the prefix from the configured list; the narrow-pane rule still drops `size` first.
- `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/tui.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`; `tests/test_tui.py`, `tests/test_config.py`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests and watch them go red.
2. Add the key and build the row prefix from it.
3. Update the docs and CHANGELOG. Mutation-check each new test.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - The full suite passes; `slicer check` passes; `slicer config tui.columns '["score"]'` then `slicer tui` shows rows without claim and size.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Worktree `.worktrees/s291`, branch `feature/s291-tui-columns`. Commit only on the branch.
